fr.elements: Open Green Space; Detached Structure; Scattered Vegetation; Open Terrain; Street Frontage; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Open Terrain; Multiple Structures
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway or road entrance that is visible from both directions of approach.
• Mark the access route to the detached structure so responders can locate it quickly without prior knowledge of the property.
• Keep the area between the main structure and the detached structure clear of parked vehicles or stored materials that could block responder movement.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Open Terrain; Grass Cover; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Near Structure; Large Trees; Limited Rear Access; Multiple Access Routes; Ground Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back any tree branches that hang directly over or within a few feet of the roof and eaves.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure so trees are not touching or nearly touching each other.
• Remove shrubs and tall grass growing directly against the base of the structure on all sides.
• Clear grass and low ground cover in the immediate area surrounding the structure, keeping it mowed short.
• Separate scattered shrubs from nearby trees so there is open ground between them and the structure.
• Clear overhanging branches along the driveway to maintain full vehicle height clearance for emergency access.
• Keep all driveway access routes free of encroaching vegetation along their edges.
• Remove dead grass, dry ground cover, and dead material from around any outbuildings or detached structures on the property.
• Clear vegetation from the rear of the structure to the extent possible to open movement and visibility around the building.
• Mow or cut grass cover in open areas immediately surrounding the structure before dry season.
